source: Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — booklet 'ដំណាំពោត' (Corn Crop), Issue 1, 2003, funded by Asian Development Bank (ADB), Loan/Grant No. 1445-CAM(SF), section V: Planting method ('ការដាំដុះ')
text:
Seed rate and pre-planting seed treatment: approximately 25-30kg of seed is needed per hectare. Before planting, seed should be soaked in warm water for 1-2 days to help the seed absorb moisture, which aids germination and root development. Seed that has been soaked should be planted within 4-6 hours to achieve a higher germination rate.

Planting can be done by two methods: manual planting (dibbling seed into holes or furrows) or by machine (mechanical planter).

Row and hill spacing, from the source's spacing table: (1) row spacing 75cm x hill spacing 30-40cm, 1 seed per hill, giving a plant population of about 33,000-44,000 plants per hectare; (2) row spacing 75cm x hill spacing 50-60cm, 2 seeds per hill, giving a plant population of about 44,000-53,000 plants per hectare.

A separate hand-drawn spacing diagram in the source illustrates planting depth of 3-5cm, hill-to-hill spacing of 30-40cm, and row-to-row spacing of 75cm — this matches the first row of the spacing table above (single-seed variant), so no numeric discrepancy was found between the diagram and the table text.

Final plant population/density depends on the germination rate achieved and may require adjustment through thinning or gap-filling (reseeding) after emergence.
